description: Category-scoped policy presets (SPEC-v3 3.6). Setting kinds: admx (an installed ADMX policy by id; values by element id, enum options by display name), registry (a documented machine policy value written to Registry.pol; for products whose templates may not be installed), audit (an advanced audit subcategory by GUID) and secpol (a security template setting). Quality updates are never deferred.

presets.name: Privacy & Telemetry
presets.hint: Required diagnostic data only, no consumer content, ads, activity publishing, web search or Recall.
presets.description: Sets diagnostic data to the Required level (the lowest supported on Pro), turns off Microsoft consumer experiences, tips, feedback prompts, activity publishing, online speech recognition, Cortana, web results in Search, clipboard sync across devices and Recall. Windows Update and security intelligence keep working. Revert from the Local GPO backup.

settings.note: Windows enforces this on Enterprise and Education; on Pro it reduces suggestions only.

presets.name: Windows Update ring: Pilot
presets.hint: Feature updates as soon as they are offered, quality updates installed within 2 days.
presets.description: The first ring for test PCs: no feature update deferral and a 2-day deadline (1-day grace period) for quality updates, so problems show up here before the other rings. Quality updates are never deferred.

presets.name: Windows Update ring: Broad
presets.hint: Feature updates 60 days after release, quality updates installed within 5 days.
presets.description: The main ring: feature updates wait 60 days so issues found in the pilot ring are fixed, and quality updates have a 5-day deadline with a 2-day grace period. Quality updates are never deferred.

presets.name: Windows Update ring: Gaming
presets.hint: Feature updates after 90 days, no restarts 10 AM-4 AM, 7-day quality deadline, drivers stay yours.
presets.description: For gaming PCs: feature updates wait 90 days, active hours 10 AM to 4 AM keep Windows from restarting during evening sessions, quality updates have a 7-day deadline with a 2-day grace period, and Windows Update stops replacing the GPU and other drivers you installed (you update drivers yourself). Quality updates are never deferred.

settings.note: You install GPU, chipset and network driver updates yourself, including security fixes.

presets.name: Defender: Microsoft Recommended
presets.hint: Advanced cloud protection, Block at First Sight, high cloud block level, PUA blocking and network protection.
presets.description: Turns on the protections Microsoft recommends for Defender Antivirus: Advanced MAPS membership with safe sample submission, Block at First Sight with a 50-second extended cloud check and the High cloud block level, blocking of potentially unwanted apps, network protection in block mode, scanning of removable drives and e-mail, and a security intelligence check before scheduled scans. Nothing here turns a protection off.

settings.note: Enabled means Block at First Sight is on.
Enabled means removable drives are scanned.
Enabled means e-mail files are scanned.

presets.name: Defender: Gaming-friendly
presets.hint: Full protection with scheduled scans at 5 AM, only when idle, at low CPU priority and a 30% CPU cap.
presets.description: Keeps every protection on (cloud protection with Block at First Sight, PUA blocking, network protection) and moves scanning out of play time: the daily quick scan runs at 5 AM, scheduled scans start only when the PC is idle, at low CPU priority and with at most 30% CPU, missed scans catch up later and security intelligence is updated before each scan. Nothing here interferes with anti-cheat software.

settings.label: Scheduled scans use at most 30% CPU

settings.note: Enabled means missed quick scans catch up.

presets.name: Defender: Strict
presets.hint: High+ cloud block level, network protection Block, every inspection parser on, PUA Block, warn turns into block.
presets.description: For PCs that should block aggressively: the High+ cloud block level with a 50-second extended check, Block at First Sight, network protection in block mode with warn verdicts converted to block, PUA blocking, script, archive, download, network file and e-mail scanning, catch-up scans, and every Network Inspection parser, inbound connection filtering, datagram processing and the DNS sinkhole turned on. Expect more false positives on unusual or brand-new programs; parsers are only ever turned on and are not reverted.

settings.note: Enabled means script scanning is on.
Enabled means behavior monitoring is on.
Enabled means downloads and attachments are scanned.
Enabled means network files are scanned.

settings.label: Every Network Inspection parser, inbound connection filtering, datagram processing and the DNS sinkhole on

presets.name: Defender: Audit / Evaluation
presets.hint: PUA, network protection, brute-force and remote encryption protection in Audit mode, to see impact before blocking.
presets.description: For evaluating impact before enforcing: potentially unwanted app detection, network protection, brute-force protection and remote encryption protection are set to Audit, so Defender logs what it would block (Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender/Operational) without blocking it. Real-time and cloud protection stay as they are. Set attack surface reduction rules to Audit in the ASR Center. Switch to the Recommended or Strict preset when the logs look clean.

presets.name: Firewall Logging
presets.hint: Logs dropped packets for the Domain and Private profiles to a 32 MB log, for the firewall log analyzer.
presets.description: Turns on logging of packets the firewall drops for the Domain and Private profiles, in %systemroot%\system32\LogFiles\Firewall\pfirewall.log with a 32 MB limit, so -FirewallLog can show what is blocked. Allowed connections are not logged (that log grows quickly; turn it on in wf.msc when building an outbound allow-list). The Public profile is set in wf.msc (Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security > Properties > Public Profile > Logging); its policy is not in the Administrative Templates.

presets.name: Attack Surface
presets.hint: No AutoRun, no multicast name resolution, no insecure guest SMB logons, no WinRM Basic authentication.
presets.description: Removes common entry points: AutoRun and AutoPlay on every drive, multicast name resolution (LLMNR, a credential-capture vector on local networks), insecure guest logons to SMB shares, and Basic authentication for the WinRM client and service. Old NAS boxes that only allow guest access stop working.

values.NoAutorun_Dropdown: Do not execute any autorun commands

presets.name: Microsoft Edge Security
presets.hint: SmartScreen and PUA blocking without bypass, typo protection, site isolation, no Basic auth over HTTP.
presets.description: Microsoft Edge policies: Defender SmartScreen and its potentially unwanted app blocking on, without the option to bypass warnings for sites and downloads, website typo protection, a process per site, blocking of dangerous downloads, and no Basic authentication over plain HTTP. Written as documented Edge policy values, so the Edge templates do not have to be installed.

settings.label: No bypass of SmartScreen site warnings
No bypass of SmartScreen download warnings
Every site in its own process
Block malicious downloads and dangerous file types

presets.name: Credentials & Authentication Hardening
presets.hint: LSA protection, NTLMv2 only, no LM hashes, no anonymous enumeration, lockout 10/10/10.
presets.description: Protects stored credentials: LSASS runs as a protected process, only NTLMv2 is sent and accepted, LM hashes are not stored, anonymous users cannot enumerate accounts and shares, elevation prompts do not list administrator accounts, and local accounts lock for 10 minutes after 10 failed sign-ins (Microsoft's baseline). Very old devices that need LM or NTLMv1 stop authenticating; some third-party plug-ins that inject into LSASS stop loading.

settings.label: Send NTLMv2 only; refuse LM and NTLM
Do not store LAN Manager hashes
No anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts
No anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares

presets.name: Remote Access Lockdown
presets.hint: Remote Desktop only with NLA and high encryption, no drive redirection, no Remote Assistance or WinRS.
presets.description: Tightens remote access without turning Remote Desktop on or off: connections need Network Level Authentication and high encryption, client drives are not redirected into sessions, solicited Remote Assistance is off, and Windows Remote Shell (WinRS) is off. Use the firewall or Settings to decide whether Remote Desktop is reachable at all.

presets.name: Removable Media & Device Installation
presets.hint: No access to USB storage and other removable storage, no AutoRun, removable drives scanned.
presets.description: For PCs where data must not leave or enter on removable storage: all removable storage classes (USB drives, memory cards, phones as storage, CD and DVD) are denied, AutoRun is off on every drive, and Defender scans removable drives. Keyboards, mice, controllers and headsets are not storage and keep working. Revert from the Local GPO backup.

settings.note: USB sticks, memory cards and phones as storage stop working on this PC.

presets.name: Audit & Logging (SOC visibility)
presets.hint: Process creation with command lines, PowerShell logging, sign-in and account auditing, larger event logs.
presets.description: Gives a SOC or incident responder the events they need: process creation with command lines, PowerShell script block and module logging, auditing of sign-ins, lockouts, account and group changes, policy changes, privilege use and system integrity, advanced audit policy enforced over legacy categories, and larger Security (192 MB), Application and System (32 MB) logs. Event volume rises; command lines and scripts in the logs can contain secrets, so protect the logs.

settings.label: Advanced audit policy overrides legacy categories

presets.name: Kiosk / Shared Device
presets.hint: No lock-screen camera or notifications, no clipboard history, no consumer content; Store off on Enterprise/Education.
presets.description: For a PC several people use: the lock screen shows no camera and no app notifications, clipboard history and cross-device clipboard are off, consumer content and tips are off, and the Microsoft Store app is turned off where Windows supports it (Enterprise and Education). For a true single-app kiosk use Windows Assigned Access.

presets.name: Developer Workstation
presets.hint: Long paths, Developer Mode sideloading and PowerShell script block logging.
presets.description: For development PCs: Win32 long paths (beyond 260 characters) for tools that support them, installing packaged apps from any trusted source and Developer Mode (needed for local app development and symbolic links without elevation), and PowerShell script block logging to keep a record of what scripts did. Developer Mode lowers protection against untrusted packaged apps; use it on development PCs only.

presets.name: Secure Gaming PC
presets.hint: Defender cloud protection and PUA blocking, no AutoRun or LLMNR, Edge SmartScreen PUA, no evening restarts.
presets.description: Security that does not cost frame rate or break anti-cheat: Advanced MAPS cloud protection with Block at First Sight, blocking of potentially unwanted apps (bundled toolbars and miners in game mods), AutoRun off, multicast name resolution off, no insecure guest SMB logons, Edge SmartScreen PUA blocking, and active hours 10 AM to 4 AM so updates do not restart the PC during play. Memory integrity, VBS and other protections stay as they are.

settings.label: Edge SmartScreen blocks potentially unwanted apps
